record.reliability_note: A community fork of AList, created in June 2025 after the AList project was sold and its ownership, docs and community were rewritten. The fork is the maintained one; AList v3 builds still run on many public instances and still work.

evidence.proved: the repository describes itself as 'A new AList Fork to Anti Trust Crisis', 25,183 stars, last push 2026-10-21
the write gate is: if !user.CanWriteContent() && !common.CanWriteContentBypassUserPerms(parentMeta, parentPath) then deny, then a second check common.CanWrite(user, parentMeta, parentPath)

the fs/list response carries Write: common.CanWrite(user, meta, reqPath) and WriteContentBypass: common.CanWriteContentBypassUserPerms(meta, reqPath); these are two different predicates and only the second mirrors the upload gate
the permission bitmask is documented in the struct comment: bit 3 is mkdir and upload, bit 8 is WebDAV read, bit 9 is WebDAV write
the AList project was reported sold in June 2025 and OpenList was created as a replacement that removes the original developer's private API links
OpenList has no paid plan and no metered allowance; the software is free to run
evidence.quote: There are currently no paid plans or commercial deployments, and the use of existing features does not involve any costs.

evidence.proved: the upload middleware answers 403 permission denied unless the user holds the write-content permission or a per-path meta override applies, so a write gate stands in front of every upload
the README states no paid plans and no cost for existing features; its text prints no quota, unit or price
evidence.quote: There are currently no paid plans or commercial deployments, and the use of existing features does not involve any costs.

evidence.proved: bit 3 of the user permission bitmask is the right to mkdir and upload, the permission that the upload gate tests first

record.notes: The one piece of this topic that can be owned outright. The source is explicit that fs/list's write field is CanWrite, a per-user exclusion-list negation, while the upload gate is CanWriteContent(bit 3) OR a per-path meta; that distinction is why a host can report write:true and refuse every PUT, and why the one writable instance in the population reports write_content_bypass:true and permission 256 with no bit 3.
